locator: Printed/PDF p31, §8 Conclusion, paragraph beginning In fact, questions about the proper scope
actual_quote:
In fact, questions about the proper scope of that theorem pro-
vided the initial motivation that led to this paper. Tait’s classical
Flyping Conjecture (first proven by Menasco–Thistlethwaite [MT93]
and later proven geometrically by the author [Ki20]) asserts that all
prime alternating diagrams of a given link are related by so-called
flype moves. Without the hypotheses of primeness, the conjecture is
false: given a nontrivial diagrammatic connect sum D = D1#D2 of
reduced alternating link diagrams on S2, one can “slide D2 along D1”
to change D into other reduced alternating diagrams of the same link,
and in general this sort of slide move cannot be achieved by flyping.
The same reasoning applies to an alternating diagram D on a surface
Σ if (Σ, D) admits a local decomposition (Σ, D) = (Σ, D1)#(S2, D2).
Therefore, the virtual flyping theorem is false without an assumption
of local primeness. What about links L ⊂Σ×I that are locally prime
but not pairwise prime?
